subsystems.name: Engineered microbe library
subsystems.role: the organisms that do the actual work of converting rock, ice and gas into living soil and breathable air.

subsystems.name: Orbital seed factories
subsystems.role: mass-produce dormant spores and cells away from Earth's gravity and biosphere.

subsystems.name: Atmosphere conditioners
subsystems.role: thicken and warm the target world's air until liquid water and photosynthesis are possible.

subsystems.name: Surface ecosystem scaffolds
subsystems.role: turn sterile ground into soil that can hold water and nutrients.

subsystems.name: Bio-feedback control network
subsystems.role: senses the planet and adjusts the biology before the system runs away.

subsystems.name: Interstellar transport layer
subsystems.role: carries seed payloads to other stars and reports back.

buildSteps.title: Design the organisms
buildSteps.detail: Genomes are synthesised and edited so microbes survive cold, vacuum, high radiation and perchlorate-rich soil, with built-in controls that stop them spreading where they shouldn't.

buildSteps.title: Test in closed microcosms
buildSteps.detail: Candidate organisms are run in sealed chambers that mimic the target world's pressure, temperature, chemistry and light for years.

buildSteps.title: Build orbital seed factories
buildSteps.detail: Automated bioreactors grow cells at scale, dry and encapsulate them into storable spores, and load them into dispensers.

buildSteps.title: Deliver the first seeds
buildSteps.detail: Landers scatter payloads across ice-rich and equatorial sites, targeting places where liquid water could exist seasonally.

buildSteps.title: Thicken the atmosphere
buildSteps.detail: Released greenhouse gases and darkening of the surface raise temperature and pressure until liquid water is stable and photosynthesis can start.

buildSteps.title: Bootstrap the biosphere
buildSteps.detail: Photosynthesis converts carbon dioxide into oxygen while nitrogen fixers and weathering agents build the first soils.

buildSteps.title: Close the feedback loop
buildSteps.detail: Sensor constellations monitor gas mix, temperature and biology; autonomous controls adjust which organisms are released to keep conditions stable.

buildSteps.title: Replicate the system
buildSteps.detail: Once one world is self-sustaining, the same orbital factories and payload designs are copied to other targets — first in the same system, then around other stars.

prerequisites.why: whole genomes can now be synthesised and edited, but not yet designed from scratch for unknown environments.
small experimental loops have recycled air, water and food for limited periods; planetary-scale ones are untested.
we can model atmospheres, but deliberately steering a whole planet's climate is theory.
no factory yet builds copies of itself without human supply chains.
nothing built can carry a payload to another star or send data back within a human lifetime.

pathway.milestone: engineered microbes used for waste treatment, carbon capture and closed life-support experiments
pathway.unlocks: reliable tools for designing organisms that survive hostile conditions.

pathway.milestone: in-situ resource use and small sealed ecosystems on the Moon and Mars
pathway.unlocks: proof that biology can persist off Earth under real radiation and dust.

pathway.milestone: regional-scale atmosphere modification on Mars, in theory
pathway.unlocks: liquid water and the first outdoor photosynthesis on another world.

pathway.milestone: one self-sustaining biosphere with human settlement
pathway.unlocks: a repeatable template for a planet-scale ecosystem.
multiple star systems' worth of habitable zones — centuries to millennia away, and only if propulsion and replication are solved.
